policy.statement: Every vitest coverage exclusion is a classified, owned, expiring debt entry. An exclusion with no owner, no justification, or a passed review date is a broken gate, not a covered file.

classifications.PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL: Cannot be measured in-process (spawned-process shims, types-only modules, build output). Requires a structural reason instead of a review date.
classifications.DEAD_CODE: No production importer. Excluded because nothing ships it. Removal is mandatory, not optional.
classifications.CONTRACT_ONLY: Imported by its own contract test only. Ships a schema, not a capability; contract tests alone never certify.
classifications.SHIPPED_SURFACE: Reachable from a shipped CLI verb, release gate, or MCP tool. The v5 GA hard gate removes every entry in this class.

policy.reviewBySemantics: A passed reviewBy fails the gate. The date is a deadline to either cover the file or delete it — never a silent renewal.
policy.defectSignatureSemantics: A SHIPPED_SURFACE entry carries EITHER `defectSignatures` (regexes that MUST still match the named source file) OR a `closureState` (the asserted defect is closed and no surface of it remains) — never neither, never both. A signature is a DRIFT ALARM, not an ADMISSION and not a defect prover, and the distinction is the one this ledger exists to keep. ADMISSION would mean the signature GRANTS coverage: that matching a regex means the file is covered. It does not — the file is not executed and no test asserts anything about it. A signature's only job is to FIRE when something about the thing the entry is about changes, so a fix forces a ledger update in the same commit. A signature that stops matching fails the gate with 'defect closed or drifted — remove or reclassify', and a signature that keeps matching proves only that nobody has touched the file. Read a pin as 'this is watched', never as 'this is licensed'. This is deliberately the same mechanism as tests/corpus/detector-hashes.json: a recorded fingerprint of source that CI diffs. PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL entries are exempt — they are evidenced by a structural reason, not by a defect.
policy.contractOnlyCeilingMeaning: Ratchet over files imported by their own contract test only. Same shape as shippedSurfaceCeiling and the same rule: the count may fall and may never rise. 6.1: these are the contracts nothing in src/ imports, so this number IS the wiring backlog, stated as a CI value rather than as a sentence. Deleting a duplicate is as valid as wiring a unique one — m40 was removed in 6.4 because `auditLanguageManifest` already answers the question it answered, a second time and worse.
policy.shippedSurfaceCeilingMeaning: Ratchet over shipped surfaces that are not PERMANENT_STRUCTURAL, not a target. The count may fall (removal, merge, real tests) and may never rise. Structural entries are excluded from the count because they are evidenced by a structural reason rather than a removable gap.

entries.structuralReason: Spawned-process entry point. A child process's istanbul report cannot merge into the parent run, so in-process instrumentation is unmeasurable. All transport logic lives in src/mcp/transport.ts and IS ratchet-covered.
entries.justification: bug-audit G6 precedent: the same structural class as dist/**. Coverage moves to tests/contract/mcp-transport.spec.ts, which spawns the real binary.

entries.structuralReason: Type-only module. Compiles to no executable code, so an instrumented run has nothing to execute.
entries.justification: Widely imported for types only; no runtime statements exist to cover.

entries.justification: No executable code paths.

entries.removalPlan: V5-090 — merge into cross-file; the shared-import + 20-char line heuristic is a partial duplicate of a covered analysis.
entries.justification: Shipped as `analyze`; duplicates cross-file and resolves finding paths against process.cwd() rather than the scan root, so a scan of a subdirectory attributes paths outside it. Merged away rather than covered.

entries.removalPlan: V5-035 — the GitHub half landed in 6.0 (least-privilege permissions, structural test). Remaining: give the GitLab and Jenkins templates a security-scope statement, then cover them.
entries.justification: Shipped as `ci-adapter`. The GitHub half of V5-035 landed: the emitted workflow now declares `permissions: contents: read` at both workflow and job level and sets `persist-credentials: false`, and tests/integrations/ci-adapter-template.spec.ts YAML-parses all three and asserts the keys. The signatures below were re-pinned by that fix, which is the mechanism working — they pinned the ABSENCE of the permissions block, so closing the defect had to break them. What is left is coverage, plus the GitLab and Jenkins templates, which still carry no security-scope statement at all.
defectSignatures:
name: QA Check
on: \[push, pull_request\]
permissions:
  contents: read

entries.closureState: CLOSED on both asserted defects (2026-09-26). The hardcoded zeros are gone — every figure is now `!== null ? … : "N/A"` — the score band reads src/reporter/presentation.ts instead of a private 60-point split, and the determination comes from the shared `decideClaim`. What remains is a rendering projection, and V5-083 has not landed.

entries.removalPlan: V5-006 — wire m26:audit into `certify` so the validators gate engineering certification, then cover the validator branches.
entries.justification: Runs inside the release gate via `npm run m26:audit`. A gate that is not covered is a gate that can silently stop working. The signatures are the schema the gate enforces: a required-field list that shrinks, or a record cap that grows without review, is the validator quietly accepting records it used to reject.

entries.removalPlan: V5-007 — single-source the version identity, then cover the drift-detection branches.
entries.justification: Runs inside `npm run version:check` on every certify. Version drift detection that is itself untested is exactly the class of defect this ledger exists to expose. The signatures are the drift rules themselves: dropping one of them would let a surface install a version that does not exist on the registry, or hand a reader a mutable tag with no way to pin it, and nothing else would notice.

entries.removalPlan: V5-038 — retire the independent HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW triage authority so classification derives from the single evidence verdict.
entries.justification: Shipped through `triage` and the MCP server. Low branch density, but it also carries an independent verdict authority that Wave 4 removes — fix the authority, then cover it. The signature is the authority itself.

entries.removalPlan: V5-080 — generate VERBS, help, README, and the site reference from one command manifest, which makes the entry point fully reachable by tests.
entries.justification: The shipped entry point. Every verb registration is a branch; a generated command manifest (V5-080) is what lifts it above the floor. The signature is the hand-written dispatch table — when V5-080 replaces it with generated code, this signature stops matching and the entry is re-reviewed rather than silently outliving its own removal plan.

entries.structuralReason: Build output, not source. Coverage is measured on src/** before tsdown emits it.
entries.justification: Generated artifacts carry no independent test surface.
